Anthropic just closed the largest capital raise in tech history, pulling in $119.5 billion from an IPO and a private placement that pulled seven of the biggest names in hardware and cloud into its cap table. The same week, the fintech world quietly consolidated: Ramp is chasing a $70 billion valuation, TPG and Corpay are taking BILL private, and Intuit is dumping Mailchimp at a $8.3 billion loss. If you build financial software, today's news is about who owns the rails and who gets to charge for them.

> Anthropic raised $119.5 billion in a single day, making it the largest capital raise in tech history.

<h2 id="anthropics-1195b-raise-rewrites-the-ai-funding-playbook"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/CD9C7JdxIoHutgXzMYtPJQ/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxhbnRocm9waWNzLTExOTViLXJhaXNlLXJld3JpdGVzLXRoZS1haS1mdW5kaW5nLXBsYXlib29rfHxodHRwczovL3d3dy5hbnRocm9waWMuY29tL25ld3MvaXBvLWNsb3NlP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Anthropic&#x27;s $119.5B raise rewrites the AI funding playbook</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/CD9C7JdxIoHutgXzMYtPJQ/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxhbnRocm9waWNzLTExOTViLXJhaXNlLXJld3JpdGVzLXRoZS1haS1mdW5kaW5nLXBsYXlib29rfHxodHRwczovL3d3dy5hbnRocm9waWMuY29tL25ld3MvaXBvLWNsb3NlP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: anthropic.com ↗</a></p>

Anthropic closed its [IPO](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/CD9C7JdxIoHutgXzMYtPJQ/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxhbnRocm9waWNzLTExOTViLXJhaXNlLXJld3JpdGVzLXRoZS1haS1mdW5kaW5nLXBsYXlib29rfHxodHRwczovL3d3dy5hbnRocm9waWMuY29tL25ld3MvaXBvLWNsb3NlP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ) of 1.127 billion Class A shares at $83.00 per share, raising approximately $93.5 billion in gross proceeds. Shares now trade on Nasdaq under "ANT." In a concurrent private placement, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and TSMC invested approximately $26.0 billion for 313.25 million Class N shares. Aggregate gross proceeds: $119.5 billion.

That private placement is the part engineers should care about. Seven companies that build the hardware and cloud infrastructure Anthropic's models run on now hold a direct financial stake in its success. That alignment changes procurement dynamics - these aren't arm's-length vendor relationships anymore, they're investor relationships. If you're building on Anthropic's APIs, expect the model roadmap to increasingly reflect what those seven companies want to sell you.

<h2 id="ramp-wants-70b-as-it-pivots-from-cards-to-ai-expense-management"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Ramp wants $70B+ as it pivots from cards to AI expense management</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: wsj.com ↗</a></p>

Ramp is in [early discussions to raise at least $1 billion](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.) at a valuation above $70 billion. That would be its third funding round in a year and more than double its valuation over that period. The pitch to investors: Ramp is no longer a corporate card company, it's an AI-powered expense management platform.

The valuation math only works if you believe the software layer, not the card interchange, is where the value accumulates. Ramp is betting that automating expense categorization, receipt matching, and policy enforcement is a bigger business than the spread on card transactions. For the engineers running finance stacks, the signal is that the spend-management category is consolidating around AI features - and the price of entry just went up.

<h2 id="bilt-wants-18b-to-move-beyond-rent-rewards"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress._dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1icmllZi10ZWNoLW5ld3MuY29t" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Bilt wants $18B to move beyond rent rewards</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress._dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1icmllZi10ZWNoLW5ld3MuY29t" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: bloomberg.com ↗</a></p>

Bilt Technologies is [seeking to raise $500 million at an $18 billion valuation](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress._dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1icmllZi10ZWNoLW5ld3MuY29t), a more than 60% jump from the $10.8 billion valuation it reached last year. The company, which built its brand on letting renters earn rewards on their biggest monthly expense, is now expanding into neighborhood-based rewards.

The strategic pivot is worth noting: rent rewards is a narrow wedge with a hard ceiling. Neighborhood-based rewards means Bilt is trying to become a local commerce platform, which puts it in direct competition with card networks and merchant offer platforms. The valuation assumes that expansion works. The engineering challenge is that neighborhood rewards require real-time merchant data integration at a scale Bilt hasn't had to handle before.

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/7ZJWT_EBnC_pvwx8H2sWaA/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHx0cGctYW5kLWNvcnBheS10YWtlLWJpbGwtcHJpdmF0ZS1mb3ItNmJ8fGh0dHBzOi8vd3d3LnJldXRlcnMuY29tL2xlZ2FsL3RyYW5zYWN0aW9uYWwvYmlsbC1ob2xkaW5ncy1iZS10YWtlbi1wcml2YXRlLWJ5LXRwZy02LWJpbGxpb24tZXF1aXR5LXZhbHVlLTIwMjYtMTEtMTkvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: reuters.com ↗</a></p>

TPG and Corpay agreed to [acquire BILL Holdings for about $6 billion in cash](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/7ZJWT_EBnC_pvwx8H2sWaA/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHx0cGctYW5kLWNvcnBheS10YWtlLWJpbGwtcHJpdmF0ZS1mb3ItNmJ8fGh0dHBzOi8vd3d3LnJldXRlcnMuY29tL2xlZ2FsL3RyYW5zYWN0aW9uYWwvYmlsbC1ob2xkaW5ncy1iZS10YWtlbi1wcml2YXRlLWJ5LXRwZy02LWJpbGxpb24tZXF1aXR5LXZhbHVlLTIwMjYtMTEtMTkvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ), offering $63.25 per share - a 31% premium to BILL's 60-day volume-weighted average price before takeover reports emerged. Corpay will invest $1.1 billion for roughly one-third of BILL and retains an option to buy the rest in 2030.

The deal follows activist pressure, workforce cuts, and intensifying competition in SMB financial software. For anyone running SMB tools, the takeaway is that the standalone SMB back-office suite is no longer a viable public company business. Going private gives BILL cover to make the kind of long-term product bets - likely AI-heavy - that public markets were punishing.

<h2 id="intuit-sells-mailchimp-for-a-third-of-what-it-paid"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/WfiQHlF0tdxkrLBjvgZ8Pw/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxpbnR1aXQtc2VsbHMtbWFpbGNoaW1wLWZvci1hLXRoaXJkLW9mLXdoYXQtaXQtcGFpZHx8aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY25iYy5jb20vMjAyNi8xMS8xOS9pbnR1aXQtbWFpbGNoaW1wLXNhbGUtYmVuZGluZy1zcG9vbnMuaHRtbD91dG1fc291cmNlPWJyaWVmLXRlY2gtbmV3cy5jb20" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Intuit sells Mailchimp for a third of what it paid</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/WfiQHlF0tdxkrLBjvgZ8Pw/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxpbnR1aXQtc2VsbHMtbWFpbGNoaW1wLWZvci1hLXRoaXJkLW9mLXdoYXQtaXQtcGFpZHx8aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY25iYy5jb20vMjAyNi8xMS8xOS9pbnR1aXQtbWFpbGNoaW1wLXNhbGUtYmVuZGluZy1zcG9vbnMuaHRtbD91dG1fc291cmNlPWJyaWVmLXRlY2gtbmV3cy5jb20" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: cnbc.com ↗</a></p>

Intuit agreed to [sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/WfiQHlF0tdxkrLBjvgZ8Pw/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxpbnR1aXQtc2VsbHMtbWFpbGNoaW1wLWZvci1hLXRoaXJkLW9mLXdoYXQtaXQtcGFpZHx8aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY25iYy5jb20vMjAyNi8xMS8xOS9pbnR1aXQtbWFpbGNoaW1wLXNhbGUtYmVuZGluZy1zcG9vbnMuaHRtbD91dG1fc291cmNlPWJyaWVmLXRlY2gtbmV3cy5jb20) in cash and stock, closing in early 2027. That's less than one-third of the $12 billion Intuit paid in 2021. Mailchimp's revenue declined 1% to $313 million in the fiscal first quarter, and Intuit's shares tumbled 15% in extended trading after management's fiscal 2027 guidance missed.

The deal is a confession: Intuit's bet that Mailchimp's email marketing would bolt onto QuickBooks and TurboTax never materialized. Bending Spoons has a track record of buying distressed software assets, cutting costs, and extracting cash flow. For engineers using Mailchimp's API, expect the platform roadmap to shift from growth features toward margin optimization.

<h2 id="banks-push-ai-agent-liability-onto-customers"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/25Q8CmK5VS3_tupoTH_mzg/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxiYW5rcy1wdXNoLWFpLWFnZW50LWxpYWJpbGl0eS1vbnRvLWN1c3RvbWVyc3x8aHR0cHM6Ly90ZWNoY3J1bmNoLmNvbS8yMDI2LzExLzE4L21vcmUtYmFua3Mtc2F5cy1jdXN0b21lcnMtdXNpbmctYWktYWdlbnRzLWFyZS1vbi10aGVpci1vd24tZXZlbi1pZi10aGV5LWdldC1oYWNrZWQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Banks push AI agent liability onto customers</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/25Q8CmK5VS3_tupoTH_mzg/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxiYW5rcy1wdXNoLWFpLWFnZW50LWxpYWJpbGl0eS1vbnRvLWN1c3RvbWVyc3x8aHR0cHM6Ly90ZWNoY3J1bmNoLmNvbS8yMDI2LzExLzE4L21vcmUtYmFua3Mtc2F5cy1jdXN0b21lcnMtdXNpbmctYWktYWdlbnRzLWFyZS1vbi10aGVpci1vd24tZXZlbi1pZi10aGV5LWdldC1oYWNrZWQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: techcrunch.com ↗</a></p>

Citibank updated its [terms of service to hold customers responsible](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/25Q8CmK5VS3_tupoTH_mzg/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxiYW5rcy1wdXNoLWFpLWFnZW50LWxpYWJpbGl0eS1vbnRvLWN1c3RvbWVyc3x8aHR0cHM6Ly90ZWNoY3J1bmNoLmNvbS8yMDI2LzExLzE4L21vcmUtYmFua3Mtc2F5cy1jdXN0b21lcnMtdXNpbmctYWktYWdlbnRzLWFyZS1vbi10aGVpci1vd24tZXZlbi1pZi10aGV5LWdldC1oYWNrZWQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ) for any activities conducted by third-party AI agents, including losses from hacks or credential leaks. JPMorgan, Bank of America, and PNC have announced similar policies, and Citizens emailed customers with the same warning. Citi exempts tools it supplies itself.

This is a meaningful shift for anyone building AI finance tools. The banks are drawing a line: their liability ends at the API boundary, and anything an agent does with the credentials is the customer's problem. That means the agent developer - you - carries the risk. If your tool leaks a credential and the customer loses money, the bank will not help. Expect this to slow adoption of autonomous finance agents and push developers toward read-only defaults and explicit human approval flows.

<h2 id="stripe-gives-ai-agents-write-access-to-treasury"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/jv-2Egw0ys8wyJJ_5a1mmA/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxzdHJpcGUtZ2l2ZXMtYWktYWdlbnRzLXdyaXRlLWFjY2Vzcy10by10cmVhc3VyeXx8aHR0cHM6Ly9zdHJpcGUuY29tL2Jsb2cvZ2l2ZS15b3VyLWFnZW50cy1jb250cm9sbGVkLWFjY2Vzcy10by1hbmFseXplLXlvdXItZGF0YS1hbmQtbW92ZS1mdW5kcz91dG1fc291cmNlPWJyaWVmLXRlY2gtbmV3cy5jb20" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Stripe gives AI agents write access to Treasury</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/jv-2Egw0ys8wyJJ_5a1mmA/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxzdHJpcGUtZ2l2ZXMtYWktYWdlbnRzLXdyaXRlLWFjY2Vzcy10by10cmVhc3VyeXx8aHR0cHM6Ly9zdHJpcGUuY29tL2Jsb2cvZ2l2ZS15b3VyLWFnZW50cy1jb250cm9sbGVkLWFjY2Vzcy10by1hbmFseXplLXlvdXItZGF0YS1hbmQtbW92ZS1mdW5kcz91dG1fc291cmNlPWJyaWVmLXRlY2gtbmV3cy5jb20" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: stripe.com ↗</a></p>

Stripe is adding [write access to Stripe Treasury for AI agents](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/jv-2Egw0ys8wyJJ_5a1mmA/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxzdHJpcGUtZ2l2ZXMtYWktYWdlbnRzLXdyaXRlLWFjY2Vzcy10by10cmVhc3VyeXx8aHR0cHM6Ly9zdHJpcGUuY29tL2Jsb2cvZ2l2ZS15b3VyLWFnZW50cy1jb250cm9sbGVkLWFjY2Vzcy10by1hbmFseXplLXlvdXItZGF0YS1hbmQtbW92ZS1mdW5kcz91dG1fc291cmNlPWJyaWVmLXRlY2gtbmV3cy5jb20), enabling them to transfer funds, convert currencies, and pay vendors within customizable limits. More than 24,000 businesses already use Stripe Treasury for agents with read access. Engineers can connect tools like Claude or Codex via Stripe's MCP server.

The design matters: agents connected through a user's Stripe account need confirmation for every action that moves money, while agents with their own API keys can work in the background under custom approval rules. A business could let an agent make ACH transfers under $50 automatically and route larger transfers to a designated approver. This is the first major payments rail to build agent-native controls rather than forcing agents through human-designed UIs.

<h2 id="chargebees-arc-automates-contract-to-billing-workflows"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Chargebee&#x27;s Arc automates contract-to-billing workflows</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: ffnews.com ↗</a></p>

Chargebee launched [Arc](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.), an agentic AI platform that turns signed contracts into proposed billing setups, drafts collections replies, and tracks how contract amendments affect recognized revenue. Teams approve proposed actions before they take effect, and citations let reviewers trace each generated value back to its source.

The citation requirement is the part that makes this usable in an enterprise finance context. Finance teams won't trust an AI that can't show its work. Arc's approach - propose, cite, approve - is the pattern every AI finance tool needs to follow if it wants to get past a pilot.

<h2 id="rogo-raises-350m-at-375b-to-automate-finance-grunt-work"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Rogo raises $350M at $3.75B to automate finance grunt work</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: bloomberg.com ↗</a></p>

Rogo Technologies is [raising about $350 million at a $3.75 billion valuation](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.), up from $2 billion in April. The round is led by Bessemer Venture Partners and General Catalyst. Founded by ex-Lazard and ex-JPMorgan junior bankers, Rogo automates repetitive work across investment banking and other finance workflows.

The doubling in four months is the signal. Investors are paying premium prices for AI tools that replace analyst and associate labor. If Rogo's tools work, the junior banker pipeline - the traditional training ground for finance - shrinks. That has long-term implications for who gets hired and what entry-level finance work looks like.

<h2 id="gtcr-circles-global-payments"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">GTCR circles Global Payments</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: reuters.com ↗</a></p>

GTCR is [exploring a potential takeover of Global Payments](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.), a payments firm it already owns 16.35% of from its Worldpay sale. GTCR is working with other private equity firms to finance the deal. If it happens, the payments landscape consolidates further under PE ownership, which historically means more aggressive cost-cutting and less investment in developer-facing infrastructure.

<h2 id="deutsche-bank-leak-exposes-582m-in-flagged-epstein-payments"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/1cR0OE6zbcdP8ZifvRUfhQ/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxkZXV0c2NoZS1iYW5rLWxlYWstZXhwb3Nlcy01ODJtLWluLWZsYWdnZWQtZXBzdGVpbi1wYXltZW50c3x8aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGF3bi5jb20vbmV3cy8yMDQ0NzIyP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Deutsche Bank leak exposes $582M in flagged Epstein payments</a></h2>

<p class="small mb-4"><a href="https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/1cR0OE6zbcdP8ZifvRUfhQ/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxkZXV0c2NoZS1iYW5rLWxlYWstZXhwb3Nlcy01ODJtLWluLWZsYWdnZWQtZXBzdGVpbi1wYXltZW50c3x8aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGF3bi5jb20vbmV3cy8yMDQ0NzIyP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source: dawn.com ↗</a></p>

A leak of over [15 million internal Deutsche Bank files](https://ecommerce-api.datafortress.cloud/r/brieftechnews/1cR0OE6zbcdP8ZifvRUfhQ/djF8d2VifDIwMjYtMTEtMjMtZmludGVjaHxkZXV0c2NoZS1iYW5rLWxlYWstZXhwb3Nlcy01ODJtLWluLWZsYWdnZWQtZXBzdGVpbi1wYXltZW50c3x8aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGF3bi5jb20vbmV3cy8yMDQ0NzIyP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9YnJpZWYtdGVjaC1uZXdzLmNvbQ), provided by two whistleblowers, exposes $582 million in flagged Epstein payments and other records involving oligarchs and sanctioned businessmen. The files were shared with journalists from more than 50 outlets and provided to the US DOJ, FinCEN, and UK HMRC.

For engineers in banking compliance, the scale is the story: 15 million files, 200 reporters, and a major global bank's transaction monitoring records in the open. Whatever controls Deutsche Bank claimed to have, they failed at the data governance level. The lesson for anyone running financial systems: your audit trail is a liability if you don't control who can copy it.
